items.title: docs(id): provider security model decision record (#5905)
items.body: Decision record for issue #5905 (task 14150) — the provider security model, settling the questions #5900 §6 expressly left to this record. ## What it decides - **Identity (D1):** a provider is its keypair in the ID object model; everything binds to the provider instance (identity, instance, manifest version) that #5900 D1 already grants against. Names are display/routing labels, never authority. - **Authenticity & admission (D2):** manifests are signed and verified at admission and on every change; admission is an explicit admin registry act; every class enters at `default_ceiling: excluded` (F13.7's client rule generalised); manifest widening re-runs admission and old grants refuse at use. - **Impersonation (D3):** addressing binds keys, never names/addresses; a registry name collision under a different key is a journaled refusal, never a rebind. - **Rogue providers (D4):** blast radius is structural (ceiling ∩ grant, bounds, classes, per-use S3 approval); removal ladder ceiling → registry → revocation, none needing the provider's cooperation; observation dishonesty named honestly as the residual risk, with attribution guaranteed. - **Bridge compromise (D5):** bridges/brokers are transport, never principals — no grants, no ceilings; compromise yields drop/delay/replay only, and replay never re-executes. - **Capability confusion (D6):** capability identity is the tuple (provider identity, capability id, manifest version); renames/re-classes mint new tuples old grants don't follow. - **Ceiling-composition audit (D7):** effective authority must be enumerable from registry + grant ledger + journal alone, with named standing audit flags. ## Boundaries kept No parent decision is changed: #5686's model, #5900's grant shape/classes/§5 invariants, #5903's embedded instantiations, and #5904's offline semantics are taken as given in §1, with an explicit conflicts check. Server/world ceiling-before-grant behaviour is preserved verbatim (task acceptance). #5931 consumed as survey input; #5898/#5899 scopes untouched. Implementation is filed as #7944 (admission signature verification, default-excluded admission, manifest-change re-admission, D7 audit enumeration), so the design does not sit without a tracked next action. Docs-only change, following the sibling decision-record format of #5900/#5904. 🤖 Queue worker lane code-u, task 14150. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? items.title: docs(id): embedded providers decision record (#5903)
items.body: Decision record for issue #5903 — the embedded (game-engine & smartphone) instantiation of the issue #5686 capability-provider model, produced under queue task 12853. What it decides (embedded face only; model mechanisms stay with issues #5898/#5899/#5900/#5904/#5905): - The signed provider manifest is the sole declaration authority; AppFunctions (phone) and ECS registration (engine) are generated projections, never reverse-authoritative. - Smartphone: id grant and Android runtime permission compose as two gates, both must pass, intersection semantics; OS revocation suspends the capability immediately. - Engine: native plugins at the trust boundary; scripted providers only inside a host-curated surface; journal (not engine replication) carries world authority. - Session-bound lifecycles: grants bind to the session instance by default and do not silently follow a provider across sessions. - Identity: device-bound delegated identity (phone), session-instance identity (engine); transports (Binder, in-process, outbound relay) carry no authority. Also records: invariants implementation must hold, the explicit parent-conflict check against issue #5686 (no parent decision changed; two parent open questions answered for the embedded classes only), alternatives rejected with reasons, and that no further splits are needed — implementation faces are owned by issues #5780 and #5781. Grounded in issue #5686 (parent model) and issue #5931 sections 2, 4, 6, 7 (field survey). Docs only; no code changes. Closes #5903 --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? items.title: doc: decision record for #5902 — terminal & website host providers
items.body: ## What Decision record for issue #5902 (design split 7 of #5686): the terminal (client and server modes) and website instantiations of the #5686 capability-provider model — sandbox and lifecycle rules, per the issue's charter. Design only; no provider implementation, per the task packet. Lands `doc/2026-11-16T09-03-20Z_decision_id5902_terminal_website_host_providers.md`, written in the family's established record shape (cf. #5901, #5903) and decided against the landed siblings (#5898 declaration, #5900 grants, #5904 offline/degraded, #5905 security) and the #5931 field survey (§1 terminal, §3 web, §6 cross-cutting). ## Decisions in brief - **D1** One declaration, per-host projections: the #5898 signed manifest is sole authority on both hosts; WebMCP registration and multiplexer/emulator state are generated projections, never reverse-authoritative. - **D2** The terminal provider is the multiplexer **session**, not the emulator surface; the typed surface is OSC 133 **command blocks** (cwd, exit status, bounded output), with raw PTY as a separate higher-sensitivity capability. Substrate is a protocol shape (tmux control-mode class), not a product; Coder AgentAPI rejected as dead (archived 2026-09-13). - **D3** Terminal sandbox = the declared envelope, stated honestly: declared cwd roots, declared environment, manifest bounds; observation is never grant-on-use; actuation is never ambient; F13.7's two-key rule in client mode. - **D4** Website provider = the page in the user's tab; calls route through the user's `id` shell for the writer-set grant check; WebMCP projection optional, the `id` extension/native-messaging channel is the always-available path; Chromium device APIs are capabilities whose absence is a declared suspension. - **D5** Lifetimes: terminal = session, website = tab (shortest in the family); grants bind to the instance and die with it by default — the same answer #5903 gave for embedded, so the family keeps one rule. The record states its two assumptions explicitly (#5899 transport profiles; F13.7 registry shape), checks parent conflicts (none; one #5899 input flagged), and closes with the rejected-alternatives table. With this landed, #5686's decomposition has one live child left (#5899). Closes #5902. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

items.title: docs(id): provider declaration model decision record (#5898)
items.body: ## Summary Decision record for issue #5898, the provider declaration model split of parent issue #5686: `doc/2026-11-11T00-18-00Z_decision_id5898_provider_declaration_model.md`. Design only; no implementation. ## What it settles - **Artefact (D1):** one signed provider manifest per (provider identity, instance) is the sole declaration artefact for every provider class; platform registries are projections. The current static `ProviderManifest` catalog in `world_caps.rs` is the degenerate case, projected into the same field shape at registry load. - **Contents (D2):** the full signed field set — identity/instance/name/`side`/kind, `epoch`, `scope`, `ttl_class`, issue/expiry, and per-capability id, contract version, typed schema, bounds, required scope, sensitivity class S0–S3, effect class — plus prohibited contents (no credentials, grants, consumer identities, code, or address-as-identity). This discharges the field spellings issue #5900's record assumed (`expires_at`, `bounds`) and the `scope`/`ttl_class`/`epoch` requirement in issue #5899's record §3.1, inside the artefact rather than a sidecar envelope. - **Signing (D3):** signed by the provider identity key over the canonical encoding; verified at admission, on every change, and at grant issuance. Admission is a separate registry record citing the manifest digest, never a countersignature. - **Versioning (D4):** three axes never conflated — `format_version`, monotonic integer `manifest_version` (immutable once filed), per-capability `contract_version` (same-major compatible) — with forward-only history and rollback refusal. - **Dynamic vs static (D5):** the capability set is static within one manifest version; availability (liveness, suspension, which version is live) is dynamic state outside the signed manifest. A changed offer is a new signed version. - **Lifecycle (D6)** and ten implementation invariants, alternatives rejected, and a conflicts check against issues #5899, #5900, #5903, #5904, #5905 and the parent record. ## Open questions routed to the parent Two questions that would fork a parent decision are recorded explicitly for issue #5686 rather than settled here: key-rotation semantics for provider identity, and federation-scope admission across administrative domains. Closes #5898. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

items.title: docs(id): provider discovery & negotiation decision record (#5899)
items.body: ## What Adds `doc/2026-11-08T09-10-14Z_design_id5899_provider_discovery_negotiation/`: the design decision record for issue #5899, settling the three questions parent #5686 left open — discovery visibility/minimisation, negotiation shape, and stale-provider handling. Design only; no code changes. Evidence base: the #5931 field survey and the current static `ProviderManifest`/`ProviderRegistry` in `pkgs/id/crates/id-core/src/world_caps.rs` (verified on origin/main `2b3ca04ac8`: static catalog only, no runtime discovery/negotiation/staleness). ## Decisions - **Discovery is a filtered view over signed declarations (#5898), tiered and minimised.** Tier A (outsider): nothing — no existence leak. Tier B (scope member, no grant): minimised card only (capability class, provider-kind class, liveness) behind a rotating, cross-scope-unlinkable discovery handle — no identity, no owner, no inventory joins. Tier C (terms/grant counterpart): full manifest for the capabilities in play only. Queries are answered from the filtered view; no existence oracle. - **Negotiation is pre-grant, authority-free metadata exchange.** Offer/counter-offer with monotonic narrowing only (widening is a protocol failure), bounded rounds, version = highest in intersection (never silent downgrade), partial agreement as a first-class outcome, typed failure reasons. It concludes in a **terms record** bound to the provider's declaration epoch; a grant (#5900) may be issued only against a live terms record and never wider than it. - **Stale handling is a TTL lifecycle, not revocation.** Heartbeat/TTL defaults per provider class (session 15s/45s, host 30s/120s, bridge-attested constrained 60s/300s); `live → suspect` (no new negotiations) `→ stale` (undiscoverable, terms void, sessions drain) `→ tombstoned` (audit). Expired caches are *unknown*, never served stale. Staleness never revokes grants; a returning provider re-declares at epoch+1. Rejected alternatives are recorded with reasons (broadcast discovery, central registry, MCP `tools/list` as the discovery layer, CapTP live-reference discovery, negotiation folded into grants, serve-stale caches, staleness-as-revocation), along with 8 implementation invariants and the explicit couplings to #5898/#5900/#5904/#5905 that this record does not re-decide. ## Tests Design document only — no code tests. Verification is coverage of #5899's three questions and its acceptance criteria, checked on this PR. Closes #5899 🤖 Queue worker lane code-d, task 12878. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.
